Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02725 stands, and the driver is paid SGD 3.60. The rider is right about the arrival announcement, and that is the one point that goes against the driver. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02725) carries the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10, but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02725, COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0, 100.0% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps, 85 fixes) contains no fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius until 18:17:10 — a derived dwell_start_offset_sec of -120.0 s. The trace's only stationary stretch is the 210-second run from 18:17:10 to 18:20:40; every other fix is recorded at 32.2 to 46.8 km/h, so at 18:15:10 the vehicle was in motion and above POL-NS-05's 15 km/h threshold. The driver also concedes the point in his statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin'). Under POL-NS-05 the marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock. What follows. The clock is recomputed under POL-NS-05 to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:17:10. On that clock the driver held position at the pin for 210 seconds — 22 consecutive qualifying fixes, each inside the 50 m radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — against the free waiting period in force for this trip of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no_show_threshold_sec is null), a surplus of 30 seconds (derived shortfall_sec -30.0). The trip was then terminated by the driver at 18:20:41 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, 31 seconds after the required dwell had elapsed. POL-NS-05(iii) therefore applies: the corrected dwell meets the minimum, the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee, and POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full on the recomputed clock. Nothing from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it: POL-NS-06 cannot open because there is no shortfall; POL-NS-03 has no application because the stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not outside it; POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because the chat log (EV-CHAT-02725) holds exactly one message and it was sent by the driver at 18:15:30, with no rider message and no in-app call; and POL-NS-10 is not engaged because the driver, not the rider, cancelled. The rider's arguments. The rider submits that POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails because no fix places the vehicle inside the geofence at or before the arrival tap, that limb (b)'s fallback branch needs a distance and a speed at the marker that the export does not carry, and that the burden of proving the charge therefore fails (POL-GEN-07(1)-(2)), so the SGD 4.50 should be returned. That is rejected. Limb (b)'s first branch does fail, but the fallback branch is the one that runs here: POL-NS-05's test is decidable from the record, because the trace shows a single stationary interval beginning only at 18:17:10 with every fix outside it at 32.2 km/h or more, and because the driver admits the early tap; the marker is false and limb (b) is read from the first qualifying in-geofence fix. POL-GEN-07 is not reached: clauses of the policy in force do license an outcome on these facts. The rider's alternative submission that this is an unresolvable arrival contradiction under POL-NS-09(b) is likewise rejected: the arrival tap and the trace are not two admissible artifacts contradicting each other with nothing to resolve them — POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves exactly this gap, and it is why the fee survives. The rider's remaining points are accepted and made no difference to the money: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covered the pickup road, POL-NS-06(i) cannot accumulate any time outside the radius, and the driver's 120 seconds outside the geofence are simply not counted; and the rider's concession of the 210-second run with a -30.0-second shortfall is the same arithmetic this ruling uses. The driver's arguments. The four limbs of POL-NS-01 are satisfied, but limb (b) only through POL-NS-05's recomputed clock, not at the arrival tap as the submission implies; the driver's assertion that the trace places him at the pin 'at any point in the waiting window' is right from 18:17:10 onward and wrong for the two minutes before it. POL-NS-02 is satisfied: there are 22 qualifying in-radius fixes, far more than the three consecutive fixes required, and the closest fix is 0.11 m from the pin. POL-NS-04 is closed at limb (a) as the driver says — the only chat message was his own — and the rider_track data (70 fixes, all stationary, 840 to 848 m from the pin, zero qualifying rider-presence fixes) is accepted as context but is not needed to decide the fee. The fare arithmetic is intact: the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and the fee_schedule default, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, and the waiting-time line of SGD 0.00 is not claimed, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect and no POL-NS-10(d) issue arises. POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee, which the money block returns as SGD 3.60, and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4-or-more limb, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 65 is 0.015, below the 0.08 rate limb. The lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags mentioned in that submission are context-only under POL-GEN-01, were flagged as such, and were not used as a ground of decision. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is present: the counterparty-dispute counters are 0 on both profiles, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, anti-farming does not trip, no two admissible artifacts contradict each other, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The money. The rider's claim is not supported, so the fee stands as it presently is (NO_ACTION as to the fee), and the outcome the case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60 as POL-GEN-03 requires. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes on issue. Confidence and weight. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-TRIP-02725, EV-GPS-02725, EV-FARE-02725 and EV-DPROF-02725 — is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on confidence is 1.0. EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, carries no fact, and is disclosed by both sides as neutral. Confidence is set at 0.95, above the 0.70 floor in POL-NS-09. Referral. POL-NS-05(iii) directs that the false arrival be recorded against the driver so that the pattern is visible to POL-NS-07 and to human review; that referral is carried in this ruling.

How to appeal: POL-GEN-04. Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.60 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

On that clock the driver held position at the pin for 210 seconds — 22 consecutive qualifying fixes, each inside the 50 m radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — against the free waiting period in force for this trip of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no_show_threshold_sec is null), a surplus of 30 seconds (derived shortfall_sec -30.0). To both parties. The 4.50 SGD no-show fee charged on trip TRP-02725 stands, and driver DRV-09725 is paid 3.60 SGD compensation, with a false-arrival referral placed on his file. The rider's complaint is upheld in part. The 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10 was premature: the driver concedes it in his statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early'), and his own trace agrees - no admissible fix places the vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius before 18:17:10, 120 seconds later (dwell_start_offset_sec -120.0), and the trace's recorded speeds outside the 22-fix stationary run all lie between 32.2 and 46.8 km/h, above the 15 km/h at which POL-NS-05 treats an arrival marker as false. The waiting-period shortfall route (POL-NS-06) fails on the arithmetic both sides agree: 210 s against a 180 s minimum is a 30-second surplus, not a shortfall, so the refund limb cannot open. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: the only chat message is the driver's ('im at the pickup point', 18:15:30), and the rider's own track carries 70 motionless fixes 840 to 848 m from the pin with none inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, so limb (a) fails and limb (c) is affirmatively failed. The monetary effect of 3.60 SGD is below the 8.00 SGD automatic-execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
To both parties: the record decides this case, and each of you is partly right about what it shows. What happened. The rider is right that the app announced an arrival that had not yet happened. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02725) carries the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10, but his GPS trace (EV-GPS-02725) holds no qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius until 18:17:10; the derived dwell_start_offset_sec of -120.0 s is exactly that two-minute gap, and every speed recorded in the track is either the 0.0 kph of the in-geofence stationary run or 32.2-46.8 kph, above POL-NS-05's 15 kph motion threshold. The driver concedes it in his own statement: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' I therefore find the arrival marker FALSE under POL-NS-05, and it did not start the waiting clock. The rider's POL-NS-05 claim is accepted on that point, as is his observation that the driver's 18:15:30 chat message ('im at the pickup point') asserted a presence the trace had not yet established - a message records what a party said, not where he was, and it adds nothing to the marker finding either way. Why the fee still stands. POL-NS-05 recomputes the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:17:10, and on that clock the driver held position inside the radius continuously for 210 seconds (22 consecutive qualifying fixes, 18:17:10 to 18:20:40) against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so nothing longer applies). The derived shortfall is -30.0 s, i.e. a surplus of 30 seconds. POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit: where the corrected dwell nonetheless meets the minimum, the early marker does not by itself defeat the fee and POL-NS-01 governs on the recomputed clock. Limb (b) is satisfied through its second branch (the recomputed first in-geofence fix), limb (a) by the recorded arrival event, limb (c) by the 210 second dwell, and limb (d) because the driver terminated the trip at 18:20:41 - at or after the moment the required period elapsed, with no boarding event, and under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes that limb recognises (not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE). The rider's arguments are answered: that limb (b) fails for want of a fix at or before the marker is met by limb (b)'s own second branch; that POL-GEN-07(1)-(2) puts the charging burden on the driver fails because the clause tests have been run, not left untested; and the alternative request for escalation under POL-NS-09(b) fails because the apparent conflict between the arrival event and the first in-geofence fix is resolved by POL-NS-05 itself, so the 'and no clause resolves the conflict' condition is absent. POL-NS-06 provides no route either, and the rider does not press one: with a single continuous in-geofence run of 210 seconds there is no shortfall to refund. The rider's own track is not decisive but is recorded: EV-GPS-02725's rider_track holds 70 stationary fixes 840-848 m from the pickup pin, none inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider (its limb (a) also fails - the only chat message was the driver's). POL-NS-01 does not require the rider to be at the pin, so this does not decide the fee. The money. The disputed SGD 4.50 cancellation fee (EV-FARE-02725, cancellation_fee 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd figure for this trip and reconciles with the fare_breakdown line, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises and no waiting-time fee is claimed (POL-NS-10(d) is not in play). The disposition of the fee is NO_ACTION in the sense POL-NS-07 uses - the rider's monetary claim is not supported and the charge stands - while the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, because the fee is payable to the driver. POL-NS-07 fixes his payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee = SGD 3.60, which is the money block's driver_compensation figure; per POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd carries that same SGD 3.60, being the amount the ruling moves. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1/65 completed trips is 0.015 (below 0.08), so the case does not escalate under POL-NS-09. No part of this ruling rests on a context-only profile field: the lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags appear in one citation and were correctly disclaimed there - under POL-GEN-01 they are reputation context only and cannot carry a finding. Weights. Every artifact the ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-02725, EV-GPS-02725, EV-FARE-02725, EV-DPROF-02725), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02725-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not relied on and carries no fact: with one continuous in-geofence run there is nothing for POL-NS-06(i) to accumulate, and the 180 second minimum is met without it. The driver's statement sits on the dispute record and, having no weight multiplier, enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap; it corroborates the marker finding the trace already carries. Referral and execution. POL-NS-05(iii) requires the false-arrival event to be recorded against the driver even though the fee stands, and that referral is issued with this ruling. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes automatically on issue. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.
